title: Alport syndrome and thin basement membrane disease

steps.tx: **Alport syndrome** is caused by pathogenic variants in COL4A5 on chromosome Xq22.3 in 85% of cases (X-linked Alport syndrome), or bi-allelic variants in autosomal COL4A3 or COL4A4 on chromosome 2q36 (autosomal recessive Alport syndrome). This established clinical parameter guides diagnostic evaluation, risk stratification, and evidence-based therapeutic management in specialized nephrology practice.

steps.tx: Pathognomonic electron microscopic finding in Alport syndrome is irregular thinning, thickening, splitting, and '**basket-weave**' lamellation of the glomerular basement membrane lamina densa. This established clinical parameter guides diagnostic evaluation, risk stratification, and evidence-based therapeutic management in specialized nephrology practice, reflecting electron microscopy.

steps.tx: **Sensorineural hearing loss** in Alport syndrome is progressive, bilateral, symmetrical, and initially affects high frequencies (2,000 to 8,000 Hz), sparing conversational frequencies in early childhood. This established clinical parameter guides diagnostic evaluation, risk stratification, and evidence-based therapeutic management in specialized nephrology practice with diagnostic threshold 2000 with diagnostic threshold 8000.

steps.tx: Pathognomonic ocular signs in Alport syndrome include **anterior lenticonus** (conical protrusion of the anterior lens capsule into the anterior chamber in 25% of cases) and central dot-and-fleck retinopathy. This established clinical parameter guides diagnostic evaluation, risk stratification, and evidence-based therapeutic management in specialized nephrology practice.

steps.tx: Early initiation of **ACE inhibitors** (ramipril, enalapril) or ARBs significantly delays onset of end-stage kidney disease and extends life expectancy by decades in both males and females with Alport syndrome. This established clinical parameter guides diagnostic evaluation, risk stratification, and evidence-based therapeutic management in specialized nephrology practice.

steps.tx: **Thin basement membrane nephropathy** (benign familial hematuria) is caused by heterozygous carrier mutations in COL4A3 or COL4A4, displaying diffuse thinning of the GBM (< 200 to 250 nm) with normal lamellation and lifelong preserved renal function. This established clinical parameter guides diagnostic evaluation, risk stratification, and evidence-based therapeutic management in specialized nephrology practice.

steps.tx: Following kidney transplantation in Alport syndrome, approximately 3% to 5% of patients develop de novo **anti-GBM** crescentic glomerulonephritis directed against the donor allograft's alpha-5 or alpha-3 type IV collagen chains. This established clinical parameter guides diagnostic evaluation, risk stratification, and evidence-based therapeutic management in specialized nephrology practice with diagnostic threshold 4.

steps.tx: **Diffuse leiomyomatosis** of the esophagus, tracheobronchial tree, and female genitalia occurs in a subset of Alport syndrome cases caused by contiguous gene deletions spanning the adjacent COL4A5 and COL4A6 genes. This established clinical parameter guides diagnostic evaluation, risk stratification, and evidence-based therapeutic management in specialized nephrology practice.
